SEO case study · Firasti

How I set up a page to be found

Evidence from the Firasti Kashmir destination page, from keyword research to a published, optimised page.

Firasti — Annotated On-Page SEO Breakdown

  1. 1SEO title: the main keyword comes first and the brand sits at the end.
  2. 2Meta description: a plain-language promise of what the page helps you plan.
  3. 3H1: one clear heading that matches what people search for.
  4. 4H2 and H3 headings: sections and day-by-day stops that mirror real search phrases.
  5. 5Image alt text: every photo gets a descriptive alt attribute.

URL Structure & Internal Linking Strategy

  1. 1URL slug: short, readable and built around the destination keyword.
  2. 2Internal links: each destination page links to the others, so visitors and search engines can follow the journey.

Keyword Research & Website Implementation

Showing Up in Google

  1. 1Page title as it appears in search results.
  2. 2Meta description that tells searchers what the site covers.
  3. 3Google’s own summary describes Firasti as a travel blog about offbeat destinations and itineraries.
Google Ads case study · Firasti

How I set up a Search campaign

A live Search campaign for the Firasti Rajasthan Travel Guide. Spend, impressions, clicks and other figures are hidden on purpose.

Google Ads — Campaign Setup

  1. 1Search campaign built around one destination, the Rajasthan Travel Guide.
  2. 2One focused ad group, so ads, keywords and landing page stay closely matched.
  3. 3Phrase-match keywords built from trip-planning searches, such as places to visit and tourist places by city.
  4. 4Campaign-level negative keywords (jobs, news, wallpaper, weather and more) filter out searches that aren’t trip planning.
Meta Ads case study · Real estate lead generation

How I run and manage Meta campaigns

Meta Ads Manager campaigns for real estate lead generation across three ad accounts. Figures shown cover 1 Aug to 23 Oct 2026.

Meta Ads — Results in numbers

  • 3,368leads generated in one ad account
  • ₹2.14 lakhad spend managed in that account
  • ~₹64average cost per lead (₹214,444 ÷ 3,368)
  • ₹26lowest cost per lead (Dudulgaon, October)
  • 62campaigns managed across 3 ad accounts
  • 21,992link clicks at 0.77% CTR and ₹9.75 CPC

Challenges I faced and how I improved results

CHALLENGE 1

Uneven cost per lead

  • Problem: in one account, cost per lead ran from ₹26 to ₹164 between campaigns.
  • What I did: compared CTR, CPC and cost per lead for every campaign, switched off the weak Charoli campaigns (₹161–₹164 per lead) and kept Dudulgaon, Moshi and the 24 Aug campaign running.
  • Result: Dudulgaon brought 1,220 leads at ₹33 each, and its October version 406 leads at ₹26.
CHALLENGE 2

Expensive markets

  • Problem: the Wagholi campaign launched on 7 Sep at ₹1,031 per lead.
  • What I did: duplicated it and relaunched a new version, the same way I reworked the Keshavanagar campaigns three times.
  • Result: Wagholi dropped to ₹616 per lead, about 40% lower, with 21 leads on a ₹1,200 daily budget.
CHALLENGE 3

One goal does not fit every campaign

  • Problem: hiring needs conversations, not property enquiries.
  • What I did: ran the Hiring campaign with a messaging objective, next to the lead-form campaigns.
  • Result: 23 messaging conversations at ₹11.93 each.

Meta Ads — Campaign Setup & Management

  1. 1Campaigns organised by project area and launch date, so each can be tracked and compared.
  2. 2Campaigns switched on, paused, duplicated and relaunched as new versions.
  3. 3Attribution setting chosen deliberately: 7-day click.
  4. 4Lead-form objective, with results and cost measured per lead.
  5. 5A daily budget set for every campaign.
  6. 6Link clicks, click-through rate, cost per click, spend, leads and cost per lead tracked for each campaign.
  7. 7A messaging-objective campaign alongside the lead-form campaigns, for a different goal.
Google Analytics 4 case study · Firasti

How I track and read the data

GA4 for the Firasti website, from setup to what the reports showed. Figures are hidden on purpose.

Google Analytics 4 — Tracking & Insights

  1. 1Data stream connected to the website and receiving traffic.
  2. 2Events recorded, including form_start, form_submit and file_download, which show lead-form and guide-download activity.
  3. 3Traffic split by channel, with Paid Search separated from organic traffic.
  4. 4Landing pages by destination, showing which guides bring people in.

What the data showed, and what I’d do next

Organic search engaged best

Visitors from organic search stayed and engaged noticeably more than visitors from paid search. Next step: tighten the ad keywords and match each ad to its destination page.

The Rajasthan page did the work

The Rajasthan guide was the only landing page that recorded key events. Next step: reuse its layout and call to action on the other destination pages.

Homepage visits, no key events

The homepage drew the most visits but recorded no key events. Next step: send visitors to the destination guides sooner, with clearer links on the first screen.
